TIJCEF Gains Global Visibility Through United Nations SDG Partnerships Platform

Tijwun Care and Empowerment Foundation (TIJCEF) has strengthened its international visibility through its inclusion on the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals Partnerships Platform. The public listing presents TIJCEF’s work to a global audience interested in practical partnerships and community-based action supporting the Sustainable Development Goals.

The development represents an important milestone for the Nigerian nonprofit organisation, which advances dignity, agency, resilience and evidence in partnership with women and young people, especially adolescent girls and underserved communities.

TIJCEF’s public profile on the United Nations SDG Partnerships Platform highlights the Foundation’s commitment to improving hygiene practices and strengthening the health, dignity and well-being of girls through simple, appropriate tools and educational materials.

The listing increases the visibility of TIJCEF’s community development approach, but it should be understood correctly. Inclusion on a public United Nations platform is not the same as receiving funding, accreditation or formal endorsement from the United Nations. It provides an international space where development commitments and partnerships can be publicly presented and discovered.

Connecting Community Action to Global Goals

The Sustainable Development Goals were adopted by United Nations Member States as a shared framework for addressing poverty, inequality, poor health, limited educational opportunities, gender discrimination, environmental degradation and other development challenges.

Although the goals are global, progress depends heavily on action within communities. International agreements must eventually translate into safer schools, better information, greater access to sanitation, improved opportunities for women and young people, and more accountable institutions.

TIJCEF’s work contributes to several interconnected goals. Its menstrual-health and school-hygiene activities support SDG 3: Good Health and Well-being. Its educational and STEM programmes contribute to SDG 4: Quality Education. Its focus on women and girls advances SDG 5: Gender Equality, while its WASH interventions relate directly to SDG 6: Clean Water and Sanitation.

The Foundation’s climate education and environmental service activities also support SDG 13: Climate Action. Its emphasis on collaboration reflects SDG 17: Partnerships for the Goals.

These relationships show why community problems should not always be treated in isolation. A girl’s ability to participate confidently in school may depend on access to menstrual-health information, suitable materials, clean water, safe toilets, supportive teachers and a school culture free from stigma.

TIJCEF’s Four-Pillar Approach

TIJCEF organises its work around four programme pillars: Dignity, Agency, Resilience and Evidence.

Dignity focuses on menstrual health, WASH, safety and the well-being of women and girls. Agency promotes education, leadership, mentoring, life skills and opportunities that help people make informed decisions. Resilience addresses climate education, environmental responsibility and community preparedness. Evidence strengthens research, geospatial analysis, monitoring, evaluation and advocacy.

Together, the pillars provide a framework through which TIJCEF can connect immediate community needs with long-term development.

For example, distributing menstrual materials may respond to an urgent need, but sustainable menstrual dignity also requires education, functional sanitation facilities, supportive policies, responsible waste management and reliable evidence about the challenges girls experience.

Building Public Credibility Through Transparency

International visibility creates both opportunities and responsibilities. As more people discover TIJCEF through public platforms, the organisation must continue strengthening its governance, documentation, safeguarding and financial accountability.

TIJCEF recognises that credibility is built through consistent action, honest reporting and respect for the people it serves. Programme figures should be supported by attendance records and activity reports. Photographs and beneficiary stories should be used with appropriate consent. Financial contributions should be documented and applied responsibly.

The Foundation’s Evidence pillar is important to this commitment. Monitoring and evaluation help TIJCEF understand whether activities are reaching intended participants and producing useful results. Evidence also enables the organisation to acknowledge limitations, document lessons and improve future interventions.

An Opportunity for Stronger Partnerships

The United Nations platform listing can make it easier for potential partners, donors, researchers and development organisations to discover TIJCEF’s work. However, meaningful partnerships require more than online visibility.

TIJCEF seeks partnerships that respect local knowledge, strengthen organisational capacity and produce measurable benefits for communities. Schools can provide access to students and support follow-up activities. Health professionals can contribute technical knowledge. Researchers can strengthen programme design and evaluation. Businesses can provide materials, technology and financial support.

Local leaders and community members are equally important because they understand the social realities that shape participation and sustainability.

Looking Ahead

TIJCEF’s inclusion on the United Nations SDG Partnerships Platform is a meaningful step in the Foundation’s development. It places a community-driven Nigerian organisation within a global conversation about sustainable development and highlights the importance of locally led action.

The milestone does not mark the completion of TIJCEF’s mission. Instead, it creates a stronger obligation to deepen impact, improve accountability and expand effective programmes responsibly.

TIJCEF will continue working with women, girls, young people, volunteers, schools and community stakeholders to advance dignity, strengthen agency, build resilience and generate evidence for lasting change.

Visit the TIJCEF website to learn more about the Foundation, explore its programmes and resources, or support the expansion of community-led development initiatives.
